voice.purpose: Agentified L01 review-only off-screen narration correction

speech_request.text:
Three notes are on the table: an attendance count, a facilitator availability note, and a room-capacity note. An assistant can turn those into a neat recommendation in seconds. But if Morgan asks, ‘Where did this come from?’ a polished paragraph is thin protection. The work needs a trail.

Our job today is small: design one preparation role and one receipt. The agent does not decide whether the session happens. It prepares a Session Option Brief for Morgan to review. That distinction matters. If we give the system a loose command like ‘run the workshop program,’ we have no useful boundary. What exactly begins its work? What can it read? What must it hand back? Who owns the outcome? These are ordinary management questions. They become more urgent when a tool can produce work while nobody is watching.

Write the job in one sentence: ‘When Morgan requests a monthly session review, prepare one brief comparing a proposed free session against the three cleared inputs.’ The trigger is Morgan's request. The output is a draft brief. The manager is Morgan. The measure is whether Morgan can check the claim and source for every recommendation without chasing the agent through a log. The forbidden actions are just as plain: no booking, no announcement, no message to participants, no spending. A useful agent job names the work it finishes and the work it leaves alone.

Now attach the receipt. Imagine the brief says the room can hold twenty people. Morgan needs to see which note supplied that number, when the brief was prepared, what the agent actually did, and whether anyone approved it. The receipt also records cost or resource use, outcome, and how to pull the draft back. A blank field stays blank and gets an owner. We never fill a gap with a confident guess. The first receipt is a handoff a busy person can understand; the engineering log can remain behind it.

In our case, approval is ‘pending Morgan.’ The outcome is ‘draft prepared, no session selected.’ The rollback is ‘withdraw the draft from the review folder and mark it superseded.’ If the source for room capacity is missing, mark the brief blocked. A complete-looking card without a source can move bad information faster than an obviously unfinished one. The receipt makes that gap visible before anyone treats the draft as a decision.

Take a moment. Picture one workflow in your own work. Keep this exercise on paper or in a local draft. Use a fictional or approved example. Do not use private operational data. What is the one useful output, and who would have to defend it?

Fill the Job and Receipt boxes. Name the trigger, permitted inputs, output, human manager, success check, and three forbidden actions. Then fill the nine receipt fields for one imaginary run. If you cannot name a source, approval state, or rollback, write ‘unknown’ and the person who must resolve it. Do not open a real system to complete this exercise. The point is to see the shape of the work before asking a tool to do it.

Save those two boxes in your Agentified Operating File as a draft. Your stop condition is simple: if the owner, source, or review gate is missing, the draft stays on paper.

existing_presenter_audio.rule: Preserve native presenter audio in these windows. Never layer synthesized narration over it.

composition_rules: Presenter footage may yield to approved teaching plates after a sentence-complete handoff.
Approved narration continues under teaching plates except during the intentional guided-work pause.
Use returned word timestamps to split the single narration source at exact segment boundaries.
Place each segment at its version-bound sequence start and fail closed if it exceeds its available scene window.
Preserve the existing 09:00 lesson duration, presenter footage, teaching plates, captions, privacy boundaries and final provider-free close.

quiet_window.rule: Only the unused remainder after the approved L01-07 narration may remain quiet.

stop_conditions: source, script, voice, identity or request hash drift
any segment exceeding its version-bound scene window
unexpected debit or cumulative project-spend breach
